compiled_state.title: [brainstorm] Phase 3 displays full epic UUID instead of user-friendly alias after epic creation
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## What

After `/dso:brainstorm` creates an epic via Phase 3 Step 1 (`.claude/scripts/dso ticket create epic ...`), the brainstorm orchestrator's user-facing summary line reports the new epic by its UUID (e.g., `3c01-3b89-21f3-485a`) instead of the user-friendly alias (e.g., `sweet-garb-oryx`).

The underlying `ticket create` CLI output already includes both forms: `Created ticket sweet-garb-oryx (3c01-3b89-21f3-485a): <title>`. The bug is in how brainstorm relays the result — it picks the UUID instead of the alias when echoing creation to the user.

## Where

`plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md` Phase 3 Step 1 (ticket creation) and Step 4 (complexity classification log line, e.g., `"Epic classified as <TIER> ... — invoking /<skill> [mode]"`).

## Evidence

In an interactive /dso:brainstorm session on 2026-05-12, the orchestrator's output line after `ticket create` read:

> Epic created: `3c01-3b89-21f3-485a`

The CLI itself had emitted:

> Created ticket sweet-garb-oryx (3c01-3b89-21f3-485a): Per-sub-branch reviewed batches for /debug-everything (sprint-parity ci-pr mode)

So both forms were available; brainstorm displayed only the UUID.

## Impact

Minor UX friction. The alias is the human-friendly identifier intended for verbal/written reference (per ticket store v3 design). Surfacing only the UUID makes it harder for the user to reference the new epic in subsequent commands or conversation without copy-pasting the long form. Downstream skills invoked by brainstorm (`/dso:preplanning`, `/dso:implementation-plan`) similarly receive and echo the UUID.

## Suggested Fix

In brainstorm Phase 3 Step 1's post-create user-facing line, display the alias (or both: `sweet-garb-oryx (3c01-3b89-21f3-485a)`). Similarly for Step 4's classification line. Apply the same pattern across any other skill that creates tickets and echoes the result to the user.
